description:
'''Rage''' (also known as '''rage music''', '''rage beats''' or '''rage rap''') is a [[subgenre]] of [[trap music]] that originated in the [[United States]] in the late 2010s. The early rage sound was characterized by short, looping, [[Stereophonic sound#Pseudo-stereo|stereo-widened]], [[future bass]]-influenced [[synthesizer]] lead hooks and basic, energetic trap [[rhythm]]s. Among the early pioneers of rage rap were [[Playboi Carti]], [[Lil Uzi Vert]] and [[Trippie Redd]]. Producer [[F1lthy]] helped develop a template for the style through his collective [[Working on Dying]] with members such as [[Bnyx]]. 

By the 2020s, the genre had developed through the influence of Carti's 2020 album ''[[Whole Lotta Red]]'', with primary production credits from producer F1lthy. Artists such as [[Destroy Lonely]] and [[Ken Carson]] on Carti's [[Opium (record label)|Opium]] label, along with [[Yeat]] and [[SoFaygo]], contributed to the popularization of the style. Mainstream artists such as [[PlaqueBoyMax]], [[Don Toliver]], [[Travis Scott]], and [[Lil Yachty]] also released rage tracks. Rage would evolve into a more extreme and experimental sound with artists such as [[OsamaSon]], [[Che (rapper)|Che]], [[Slayr]], [[Nettspend]], [[Prettifun]], [[Edward Skeletrix]], [[Bleood]], [[2Slimey]] and [[Lucy Bedroque]]. This style was defined by the use of bass heavy and distorted [[Tr-808|808s]], [[Rap metal|screamed]] [[Auto-Tune|autotune]] vocals and aggressive production.  

Underground rappers such as [[Tezzus & Diamond*|Tezzus]], [[Nine Vicious]], [[Yung Fazo]], [[Yung Kayo]], [[Ian (rapper)|Ian]], and [[1300Saint]], alongside rap collectives [[Ø Way|ØWay]], [[List of Internet rap collectives|Slime Krew]], and [[Young Vamp Life|YVL]] would also release rage tracks. The genre has been cited as an influence on the development of the 2020s [[UK underground rap]] scene, influencing artists such as [[Lancey Foux]], [[Fimiguerrero]], [[Fakemink]], [[EsDeeKid]], [[zukovstheworld]], among others.
